core_obligations: Normalise the generating data: write F as generated by sections s_i over quasi-compact opens, decompose the opens so that each s_i becomes a constant section n_i, discard zero generators, take absolute values, and for every subset of indices add the intersection of the corresponding opens with the gcd of the corresponding integers; conclude that at every point the gcd of the active generators is attained by one of them (proof lines 3504-3516).
Define the filtration by the positive integers, with the n-th piece generated by the generators whose value is at most n, and note that for n large it equals F (proof lines 3518-3522).

Identify the successive quotient: it is generated by the single value n over the union of the opens with value at most n, and the kernel of the map from the extension by zero of Z over that union is generated by the same value over the smaller union, which gives the required short exact sequence (proof lines 3522-3527).
proof_roadmap: Successive quotients and their short exact sequences (proof lines 3522-3527).
difficulty_reason: On a space where the intersection of two quasi-compact opens is quasi-compact, the lemma shows that a subsheaf of the constant sheaf Z generated by finitely many sections over quasi-compact opens admits a finite filtration whose successive quotients sit in short exact sequences involving extensions by zero of the constant sheaf Z along inclusions of quasi-compact opens (statement lines 3479-3501). The proof is a real normalisation argument: after decomposing the generating opens so that the generators become constant sections, removing zero generators and flipping signs, the author enlarges the list by adding, for every subset of indices, the intersection of the corresponding opens together with the greatest common divisor of the corresponding integers, so that at every point the gcd of the generators active there is attained by one of them (proof lines 3504-3516). The filtration is then indexed by the positive integers, with the n-th piece generated by the generators not exceeding n, and the successive quotient is generated by the single value n over the union of the opens where the generators are at most n while its kernel is generated by the same value over the smaller union, which produces exactly the required short exact sequence (proof lines 3518-3527). The claim is H2: the gcd-enlargement device and the filtration by values are both written out in full.
